taken by it given that it was essentially a development of the style that had dominated English football in the80s klopp stands as the high priest of gagum pressing although his example has been followed at Dortmund by Thomas tul while the theory is a key tenant of such coaches as Pep Guardiola Marcela beela and Mario poccino pressing developed in the 60s in the USSR and in the Netherlands and was characterized by multiple players closing down the man with the ball that inevitably left other players free but the reasoning was that that didn't matter because a player Under Pressure would be unable to hit a long accurate pass to find an unmarked teammate it spread to become a defining feature of British and Scandinavian football by the mid '70s gag and pressing is a development aimed specifically at winning the ball back as soon as it has been lost a player who has just won the ball is vulnerable because he may still be getting the ball under control he has just expended energy in the challenge and he may not have had time to fully appreciate the distribution of his teammates and opponents on the pitch there are variations some coaches yup hus in his days at Bayern for instance send one man to the ball While others close down potential recipients of the pass klopp tends to surround the man with the ball and Guardiola seems to prefer blocking the passing Lanes between the man in possession and potential recipients but all rely on speed and organization looking to panic the man on the ball and regain possession as quickly and as high up the pitch as possible countering the Counterattack the biggest problem for all of them is knowing when to stop when a team should stop hunting the ball and should fall back into defensive shape so effective has the tactic been that the proportion of open Play goals scored on the Counterattack in the champions league has almost halfed in the last decade in practice gagan pressing is often targeted in the recent game against Tottenham for instance Liverpool made a clear point of sending their forwards to close down the central Defenders looking to force a pass to Danny Rose of fullback who was then hounded on mass Rose presumably had been identified as the fullback slightly less comfortable on the ball and was vulnerable because with the goal line behind him and the touch line to his left he is cornered this is why Louis vanal title: What is a False Nine?
content: The false nine is a deep lying striker who drifts away from the center backs into a danger area between the lines creating uncertainty in the defense about whether to track or stay. While the term was popularized by Pepgardiola's use of Lionel Messi in the role with Barcelona and Ces Fabregas's similar function for Spain at Euro 2012, the idea that a striker can cause havoc between the lines was popularized by the so-called Denube school in the 1930s and was also used by the magical Maguyars of the 1950s. Traditionally, the number nine has always been football's center forward. numbers originated with two games in 1928 when Sheffield Wednesday played Arsenal and Chelsea played Swansea Town. In both instances, the nine took up the central most advanced position in the 235 formations. While numbering varies across continents in defense and midfield, nine is an accepted shorthand for a team's central striker. A normal nine leads, playing on the shoulder of the defense or holding up the ball and looking to bring midfielders in or a deep line striker into the game. Their role is to score to get on the end of crosses or feed off through balls. The traditional nine is a focal point leading the game and playing against the center backs trying to find space in behind them. Matias Cindelar, a willowy creative striker who played for the Austrian national side in the 1930s, was probably the first famous false nine. Although Jonathan Wilson notes that a deep dropping center forward was reasonably common across central Europe in the 1920s, and it was also a feature of riverplate sides in the same era. Cindela's frame was not ideal for the physical man marking utilized by sides at the time. And so he dropped off to find space and bring his wingers and inside forwards into the game. Nandor Hiduti did the same for one of the finest teams ever, the Hungarian side of the 1950s. Both players famously terrorized English national teams used to playing against a physical but immobile traditional number nine. The false 9 is rather obviously not a traditional nine. Pep Guardiola used Messi as a false nine as part of his positional play theory. Best summed up as creating superiorities between lines of pressure through rehearsed movements and rapid passing. Rather than use a striker as a focal point, Guardiola instructed Messi to drop deeper while his wingers either came infield or stayed wide depending on where the ball was. This created at least a triangle, if not a diamond, of available passes for the midfielder in possession. At least one of the passing options was between the lines of the opposition midfield and defense. Lucas Bleti's Roma side in the 2006 2007 season used Franchesco Tati as a sort of false line before Messi, but he was more of a creating attackive midfielder who had striking duties rather than a striker who dropped off. Nonetheless, Roma's fluent attacking that season was a likely prompt for tacticians who wanted to exploit the potential of overloads between the lines. False 9 can be devastating with the right personnel. Whilst most modern teams have swapped man marking for zonal marking, the movement of the false 9 will create a problem for any back line. Either a center back pushes up, which isolates his partner, dragging in a fullback to cover or leaving an exposed space, or he leaves the false 9 to drop, allowing him space and time to pick a pass or shoot. A midfielder could drop to pick up the false N, but that creates another overload further up the pitch. Either way, players who find space and receive the ball between the lines will cause problems for the opposition. While a greater need for compactness, the rise of pressing and the return of three or fiveman defenses has seen fewer pure false nines in recent seasons, the best center forwards such as Diego Costa and Zlatan Ibrahimovic have incorporated dropping off to find the ball in their repertoire. Indeed, it's fair to say that the new real nine has been significantly influenced by its false cousin. If even Andy Carol can learn to drop deep, the days of the classic number nine might just be over. Whiskey every night. I'm smoking every day.

content: Playmakers come in many different forms the most overt differentiation is depth the classic 10 called the enganche in Argentina atatia in Italy and Amir Amado or mayor at acante in Brazil versus a deep Ling playmaker sometimes referred to as a regista in Italy in the classic Argentine 4312 the primary playmaker in the whole is called and inun which translates as hook football in Argentina morphed from a 433 in the 1970s to a 4312 in the 1980s the 433 saw a central solidly defensive midfielder whose job it was to spoil flanked by a slightly more advanced box-to-box player have adapted to counter this system and now Mark the creative player playing in the hole this obsolet as teams playing with four 42 or 4231 could exploit overloads out wide to circumvent the 4312 has title: Total Football Explained
content: It's probably fair to say that no style of football has had as much influence on the modern game as Total Football. The style is most associated with the Ajax and Dutch national teams of the 1970s, and in fact, it got its name from the 1974 Netherlands World Cup side. But it had its roots in the Austrian national side of Matthias Sindelar in the 1930s, and Ferenc Puskas and Co.'s Hungarians in the 1950s. And the lineage of Ajax's way originated with two English coaches, Jack Reynolds, who managed the club in three spells between 1915 and 1947, and Vic Buckingham, who managed them twice between 1959 and 1965. Then came the pairing who really created the style, Rinus Michels, who had played under Reynolds and replaced Buckingham in the dugout, and Johan Cruyff, perhaps the most significant figure in European football ever. It was then continued by Stefan Kovacs, under whom Ajax became the greatest club side in the world for a time. Total Football has perhaps two key concepts, the utilization of space and the fluidity of positions. Both were aided by Michels' fanatical work rate and discipline, with fitness a significant focus alongside skill work with the ball. Space is key. Make the pitch big when you're attacking and small when you're defending. In order to make this work, Ajax also pressed. At times, they pressed almost manically. There was less an emphasis on pressing into passing lanes than an effort, often led by the wonderfully tenacious Johan Neeskens, to swamp the opposition player in possession. In order to facilitate this, Ajax also played a very high defensive line, compressing space yet further. The formation most associated with Total Football is the 4-3-3, becoming a 3-4-3 as the libero steps up into midfield, a feature that persisted in Dutch football with players like Barry Hulshoff, Horst Blankenburg, and Danny Blind, and started largely at Ajax by the Serbian Velibor Vasović. This allowed the defense to begin attacking moves, but also ensured that there were spare markers for the opposition center forwards, and that Ajax could match a four-man midfield. As Jonathan Wilson notes, while other sides had engaged in horizontal positional such as wingers dropping inside or mild vertical ones like Nandor Hidegkuti, Ajax and the Dutch national side were the first to engage in wholesale positional switches up and down each flank. In this way, the 4-3-3 or the 3-4-3 saw players on either flank push up and drop off, fluidly interchanging to create baffling attacking patterns. The team's spine in the most successful period of the early 1970s was Blankenburg, Neeskens, and Cruyff. With Heinz Stuy in goal, the wide players Wim Suurbier, Arie Haan, who later became an accomplished sweeper, and Johnny Rep on the right, and Ruud Krol, Gerrie Mühren, and Piet Keizer on the left all swapped with each other, knowing that this spine would hold and cover. But, Cruyff also dropped off and moved wide at will. Pressing meant that as long as players were pushed up and everyone could defend as well as attack, the fluidity of the team did not compromise its defensive shape. Of course, the attacking system could be negated as Berti Vogts and West Germany showed in 1974 by aggressive man-marking and flooding the midfield, but when Ajax were on song, it was nigh on impossible to stop them. The influences of Total Football show up in the coaching of Marcelo Bielsa, and via Michels and Cruyff's spells at Barcelona in the positional play of Pep Guardiola. Guardiola's positional play, which relies on vertical overloads, is only possible if players can change positions. And both Bielsa and Guardiola encourage their teams to control space, interchange, press, and have encouraged players to play in roles that they aren't used to, where their skills as midfielders allow them to be attack-minded defenders, for example. The legacy of total football is not just in the beauty of Ajax and the Netherlands in the '70s. It lives on in some of the best football of today. title: Catenaccio Explained
content: There is no style of football so notorious as katanacho. Perhaps no style so misunderstood. Nowadays there is a tendency to use katanacho when referring to any defensive style of play, but its meaning is quite specific and arguably not necessarily defensive. It began in Geneva in the 1930s with Sevet and their Austrian coach Carl Rapan. Sevet was semi-professional and often struggled against fitter, fully professional foreign opposition. Rapan's solution was to adopt a more defensive approach, looking to absorb pressure before soaring forward on the counterattack. Most sides in central Europe at the time played a 235 formation. Although in practice the two inside forwards would be slightly withdrawn. What Raphan did was to pull back his two wing halves to flank the fullbacks forming a back four with the center half and inside forwards creating a midfield three. The primary function of the withdrawn wing halves was to combat the opposition wingers. The two fullbacks then became in effect central defenders, playing initially almost alongside each other. Although in practice, if the opposition attacked down their right, the left of the two would move towards the ball with the right covering just behind and vice versa. In theory, that always left them with a spare man, the bolt. Raphan became coach of Switzerland and instituted the system with great success. Switzerland beat England in a friendly shortly before the 1938 World Cup and then beat Germany in the first round of the tournament itself. But it was when the system moved to Italy after the war that it really took off. The romantic explanation is that the Salonitana coach, Jeppi Vani, pondering his defensive problems on an early morning walk by the coast, was inspired by seeing a twler using a reserve net to catch the fish the first net had missed. The truth may be more prosaic. There was significant Swiss influence on Italian football in the 40s and 50s, but Vani was the first to use the idea of the extra man at the back with success in Italy, leading Salonatana to promotion in 1947. That inspired others. Naria Roco used the system at Triestina and then at AC Milan with whom he won the European Cup in 1963. But it was at International Helenia Herrera who became its greatest exponents. By then the system was known as katanacho, a term that refers to the chain on a door. Il Grande in played a lopsided system. The right back tucking in as a marker with the right winger Jer shuttling back as cover while the left back the great Justinto Feti was encouraged to get forwards. They won the European Cup in 1964 and in 1965 before falling to Jocken Celtic in the 1967 final. An epic game that showed that allout attack could still overwhelm allout defense.

title: Liverpool's Counter-Pressing Explained

title: What is a Raumdeuter?
content: What is a Raumdeuter in football? Well, the term was invented by Thomas Müller, who's one of its most famous examples. As players, Raumdeuters are sometimes hard to define, both linguistically, because there's no direct translation from German, although space interpreter is probably closest, but also literally, because it's hard to always see what they do on the pitch. Because rather than executing eye-catching passes or flashy finishes, a Raumdeuter identifies and exploits space. Their expertise is being in the right place at the right time. Raumdeuters operate in between the defensive lines. They love to attack vertical channels between opposing defenders, and they are masters of creating space through deception. This requires excellent anticipation, movement, and spatial awareness. And it's these abilities that make them so hard for opposition defenders to spot.

title: What is an Artificial Transition?
content: What is an artificial transition in football? Well, you've probably heard the word transition, which is when possession is regained by a previously defending team or lost by a previously attacking team. Coaches love them because they catch opposition teams out of their shape. But the problem is that you need to have lost the ball in order to win it back to start a transition. And if you can't win the ball back, then there's a risk that the opposition will score. So, what if you never lost the ball at all? This is where the artificial transition comes in. The team on the ball look to bait the opposition out of their defensive shape and into a high press through things like wall passes or standing provocatively with their studs on the ball. Once the opposition are out of their structure, the team on the ball will pass quickly to exploit the spaces left behind. The opposition are now caught in transition without possession ever needing to change hands.

title: The Return of the 4-4-2
content: by the time the 21st century swung around the go-to formation that had reigned Supreme throughout the 80s and 90s the 442 had started being superseded by more complex structures on the football field fast forward to present day though and the 442 is making something of an unlikely re-emergence within the world of football so could it be that we're seeing its return it's impossible to say precisely when the 442 formation materialized as a credible tactical structure within the world of football its direct ancestor the 4-2-4 formation has precedence both in Hungary and Brazil and the historian of football tactics Jonathan Wilson points out that the 4-2-4 shape was an inevitable development given the structures that were being used worldwide at that point in time it wasn't long before the 4-2-4 went mainstream the Brazil National Team used it to win their first World Cup in 1958 and then again in 1970 but in the early 60s Soviet Coach Victor maslov made The Tweak that turned the 424 into a 442 dropping the wide players in the front four alongside the two Central midfielders now part of the enduring popularity of the 442 structure comes from its capacity to divide up space functionally at a time where zonal marking systems were gradually replacing the man marking systems that had been used the 442 offers a nice base in which to defend and also gives scope for possessional structure which has a lot of flexibility the two Strikers can push onto the opposition center-backs providing a threat in the Box the two wide midfielders can push up and isolate themselves against the opponent's fullbacks looking to find the strikers in the box with crosses and the central midfielders can arrive late to add an additional thread it was this setup that led Sir Alex Ferguson to the treble in 1999. Andy Cole and Dwight Yorke as a strike partnership serviced by Ryan Giggs and David Beckham on the wings with Paul skulls pushing forward an attack protected by Roy Keane in behind But as time went by the 442s started to fall out of fashion in the early 2000s teams were looking to possess the ball more and the use of two Strikers meant that teams playing the 4-4-2 could only field two Central midfielders teams who wanted to possess the ball now started to drop one of their Strikers deeper so that they could have an overload against two-man Midfield and before long everyone was adopting the 4-2-3-1 even now 20 years later most teams set up with a lone Striker but that doesn't mean that the 442 is dead and of course there are proponents of the 442 in the present day Diego Simeone has made a name for himself playing out of the 442 structure and unite Emery has a lot of success with it too but there is a form of 442 that's being used across elite football and you might not even have realized it and that is the 442 press because although 442 largely went out of fashion as an in-possession approach it never really went away as an out of possession structure and there are a number of reasons for this primarily as we have said it offers a really nice shape out of which to defend it gives good coverage across the pitch the two players in the first line can control the opposition backline and build up and then behind them the two Banks of four offer good protection you can also use the wide midfielder and fullback to give you double coverage on the opposition wide player on either side of the pitch or if you want to you can push your Winger higher up to press on the opposition fullback 442 shape is also easy to segue into from other possessional structures for example in 4231 the number 10 can push up alongside the striker and the wired players drop alongside the central midfielders or out of a 4-3-3 the wide forwards can drop in and one of the eights can push up alongside the striker both Manchester City and Liverpool have used this sort of out of possession shape in recent seasons the 442 structure also lends itself well to Mid blocking when teams use a mid-block they sit slightly deeper and allow the opposition possession into their own half but when they hit a point around the halfway line they will start to put the opposition under pressure the coverage offered by a 442 shape makes it the ideal setup for this sort of approach so as the 442 formation became less popular in possession it never really went away as an out of possession approach and in the intervening years as out of possession structures have become increasingly important in the modern game the 442 has seen something of a Renaissance given the sort of flexibility that it other types of lazy stereotyping are added it also means that we become absolute in our assessment of players they are a winger rather than they play out wide and are expected to get close to the goal title: How Goal Kicks Are Changing Football
content: a quiet Revolution is happening in football and at the heart of it is a recent rule change this is how Over The Last 5 Years goal kicks have completely changed the sport there are an average of 16 goal kicks in a Premier League match making it the third most common set piece behind throwin and free kicks and yet until 2019 goal kicks had largely been taken without much thought on most occasions teams pushed everyone up and the goalkeeper smashed the ball as far as he could then in summer 2019 ifab changed the rule around goal kicks meaning that the ball no longer had to exit the penalty area before a player could receive the first pass it was Radical the number of goal kicks being taken short has more than doubled since 201819 in the Premier League but in the past 5 years the law Chang has birth a range of Trends including hastening the rise of man-to-man marking the hollowing out to Central Midfield and the tactic of playing over the opposition press those three themes were highlighted by uefa's technical review of the 2024 European Championship examples included Slovakia luring England into a full press and almost scoring via direct play up to their Striker and the Netherlands creating an overload in the middle of the pitch against High pressing Austria the impact of the rule change was underestimated by many said arson Banger the former Arsenal manager who is now chief of global development for FIFA World football's governing body in a review of the rule last year it was introduced to make the game faster and more spectacular but even more has changed the main attraction is to attract your opponent as far away from their goal as you can and try to play through if you can play through the first pressure you have a whole half of the pitch to be dangerous but how does a trend like this start to proliferate in such a quick space of time and how has it become just as normal to see a center back passing the ball to the goalkeeper as the other way around that's something Arsenal regularly do with Defender Gabriel playing to keeper David Rya before the latter punts long towards Kai ht's up front with Mikel aretas Midfield racing forward to support the one side of the pitch now with a Defender and goalkeeper able to exchange passes inside the Box possession remains dead Central most teams bring midfielders to the box now and it just makes the space much bigger to defend says an analyst at a major European Club it is so hard to be compact as if you want to get pressure on at the top end the midfielders are having to match midfielders which naturally opens up space behind them the question you are asking the opposition is are you so Keen to get pressure on us that you're going to leave yourself 3v3 or 4v4 at the back teams realize they have to commit more bodies to force it long which explains the rise of man-to-man pressing one of the most effective teams in the first few seasons after the rule change were Italy's Inter Milan under Antonio Conte Conte prefers rehearsed passages of play and took advantage by constructing moves that ended with long balls that forwards could run onto Germany's national team have been creative in their use of goal kicks in this example against the Netherlands in March 2024 goalkeeper Manuel Neuer edges forward with the ball while his midfielders move out from the center to drag their markers wide and open up a central passing channel to HTS the ball from Neuer is the trigger for The Supporting Cast to coals around him with ht's layoff springing a 4v4 opportunity the new rule gave coaches a blank canvas to work on and has produced many variations in how to try to gain an advantage in buildup Southampton manager Russell Martin has been among them in this example from a game against stands still with the ball and delay his pass until the very last moment and Center back Thomas Bean is trusted to dribble across his own penalty area and wait for the space to present itself there subsequent Seasons it has been rising to the point where in 2324 so far 20.6% of Corners have been taken short up from 7 1.7% in the previous year and since the vast majority of Corners are still of corners and a rise in the number of goals from Corners doesn't necessarily mean that one has caused the other it is possible but equally it could just be that teams are thinking more carefully and working more specifically on what they do with long corners for what it's worth 24 of the 150 one goals scored after Corners last season were from short corners while this season it's three from 29 title: What Actually is Rest Defence?
content: foreign you might not think that a friendly match could anger a manager but when Eric ten Hogs Manchester United lost two Cadiz in a mid World Cup game at the end of 2022 he was noticeably annoyed in the post-match press conference he didn't hold back Cadiz were a threat in transition he said for the second goal we were not awake we had a bad rest defense especially in the Midfield it's unacceptable the phrase rest defense is creeping into the English football vernacular more and more managers are mentioning it in the course of their media duties tenag is probably the most high profile user of the term in the Premier League but the big question is what does it mean what is rest defense if you break football down into its constituent Parts it can be reduced to two basic phases of play in possession and out of possession usually when a team are in possession of the ball they'll be looking to move the ball towards the opponent's goal in a bid to score you could call this the attacking phase when a team are out of possession they will generally be looking to stop the opponent from moving the ball closer to their goal so as to make it harder for them to score you could call this the defensive phase there are of course outlier situations in both phases but between these two phases of play you have the most basic moments in football but these two phases are opposite sides of the same coin if a team is not in possession then they are out of possession by definition if they lose the ball when they're attacking they're now defending and it's this phenomenon of teams shifting between in possession and out of possession phases of play but offers the context to understand rest defense because for any team that's in an attacking phase there's always the possibility that they lose the ball and enter the defensive phase and the question that rest defense seeks to answer is how well prepared are you in the attacking phase to deal with that shift to defending the phrase rest defense is actually a translation of the German phrase rest vetidigan this is a portmanteau word that is built from two separate words the word vetidigan means defense and the word rest translates directly into English but there's an etymological problem here where a native English speaker hears the word rest they will most likely associate it with the verbal form of the word word that is relaxing or putting less effort in German though its usage is noun or it refers to the idea of what is left over the remainder so in an attacking phase a team will commit a number of players forward to try to score a goal the rest of rest defense literally refers to the players that are left over the non-attacking players during their attacking phase rest defense refers to the defensive attitude of these non-attacking players and asks how are these players set up in order to best deal with a turnover of the ball this is rest defense in its simplest form so when Eric tenhar complains about his team's rest defense what he's referring to is the positioning of his players within the attacking phase that's led to the opposition being able to cause Manchester United problems in those moments when the ball was turned over and a counter-attack was sprung if United's rest defense had been better tenharg was suggesting then these transitional moments would have been less dangerous so why are we hearing more and more Elite managers referencing rest events in the present day well the answer is fairly simple we've already established that rest defense refer first to A team's defensive structure in the attacking phase but the best way of being an attacking threat is to push more players forward if you do this though you're moving players further away from your goal and weakening your defensive structure if the ball is turned over you can only commit to pushing more players forwards then if you're confident that the players who are left over the rest defense are up to the task of covering the opposition in the event of a counter-attack for elite managers like Pep Guardiola Julian nogglesman or of course Eric ten hark A team's attacking threat stands or falls on the ability of their rest defense to offer their attacking unit protection these managers need to maximize their scoring potential and so in order to achieve this they need to make sure their rest defense is perfect so to reverse the old adage and co-opt it slightly you could say that rest defense is the best form of attack if you like this video please consider subscribing to the channel title: What's the Lavolpiana Build Up?
content: You might have noticed that some big Premier League teams have started using more traditional overlapping fullbacks with the defensive midfielder dropping in between the center backs to help with buildup play. Arsenal, Liverpool, and Manchester City have all been using this tactic. It's known as the Lavalpiana buildup and it's credited to one of Pep Guardiola's lesserknown influences, Ricardo Lavalpe. Having been a goalkeeper during his career, Lavale was interested in playing out from the back by creating overloads in the first line of his buildup. To do this, he would drop an extra man into the back line to create more celas or exits. Levulp became manager of the Mexican national team in 2002. And in 2005, Guardiola made the final move of his club career to Mexican side Doroseloa and watched on as Levulp implemented his signature buildup. Less than 2 years later, Guardiola was using the same buildup at Barcelona B before going on to influence so much of modern football

content: you can now get a 30-day trial to experience the athletic for free visit the link in the description below to try it now the 433 formation has become the formation of choice for many of the top sides in european football with its modern adaption best attributed to renus michels and the total football of his dutch national teams of the early 1970s a formation often deployed by former ix and barcelona manager johan cruyff it became perhaps most famous during pep guardiola's magnificent tenure at barcelona and has also been one of his preferred setups during his time at manchester city another beneficiary of the 433 is liverpool's jurgen klopp who have also seen great success while utilizing this structure although with a different style of play not to be limited to club football the 433 has also left its mark on the international scene with successful national teams such as 2010 world cup winners spain and the recent european champions italy also choosing to implement the formation it's typically seen as an attacking formation and often used by coaches who look to dominate the ball but while it has strengths there are also weaknesses too the 433 is the formation most associated with positional play with one deep lying midfielder two attacking midfielders two wingers and a striker to go along with the back four occupying the five vertical channels synonymous with positional play occurs seamlessly throughout the attacking phases it also helps in the creation of natural triangles all over the pitch always offering the ball carrier a simpler passing option when a triangle is created among three players the player in possession will in theory have a minimum of two short passing options making it easier to retain possession of the ball it also offers aside simple solutions for positional rotations for example the fullback overlaps the winger tucks inside and the ball-sided attacking midfielder can then cover the run of the fullback by dropping out wide another very common rotation in the 4-3-3 is when the deep-lying midfielder drops down between the central defenders creating a back three and allowing both full-backs freedom to push forwards into the attack in a 4-3-3 the ability to play with three central midfielders is one of its greatest strengths and is also one of the main reasons behind its popularity while a classic 442 offers only two players in central midfield the 433 allows for an extra player in the middle of the park and has the potential to create numerical advantages in central areas against opposition sides only using two central midfielders and the fluidity of the 433 also offers tactical flexibility when out of possession whether defending in a 4-3-3 shape or dropping the wingers to create a 4-5-1 both options offer different problems for the opposition to solve a team maintaining the 4-3-3 shape with the wingers in the same line as the striker requires its wingers to play extremely narrowly this helps to keep the team shape compact and to avoid the opposition being able to play line-breaking passes through the middle when the wingers drop into the midfield line to create a more conservative 4-5-1 block the team will often defend from a deep position on the field applying less pressure higher up the pitch while the 433 offers a good starting point for dominating the ball and recovering possession quickly through counter pressing some of the strengths of the system may also be some of the perceived weaknesses though having an attacking line of three players is useful to overwhelm the opposition when in possession any lack of defensive discipline from the front three can quickly be taken advantage of whether defending in a block or transitioning to defense from attack the ability of the front three to recover and get back into shape is vital interestingly enough employing a front three compared to a front two may sometimes make the formation less of an attacking threat in the final third in these scenarios the striker may become isolated if both wingers stay wide or if neither of the attacking midfielders push forwards and make a late run into the box so while the fluidity of the shape in possession can make it difficult for the opposition to defend and control dangerous spaces it also increases the complexity of decision making and positioning for the central midfielders both attacking midfielders and the 4-3-3 will often find themselves in situations where they must quickly make decisions on whether to push forwards and join the attack or remain deeper to offer balance to the side playing with a single pivot player also increases the demand for discipline and positioning for that defensive midfielder as they will have more spaces to cover to protect the backline there is no question that the dominant barcelona sides under pep guardiola have increased the interest surrounding the 433 and infatuation with the system has only increased since his arrival in the premier title: A Guide to 4-4-2
content: for black friday you can get the athletic for only one pound a month for a whole year see the link in the description now to sign up one of the most traditional formations in football the classic 442 has fallen out of favor with many of the top sides around the world this system was previously widely used across football where it saw much success under italian manager irigo saki at ac milan in the 1980s with a focus on compactness and pressing without the ball and wing play when in possession from the 1980s and into the 90s some of the most successful clubs in england were also utilizing the 442 between ferguson's famous man united teams and arsenal's triumphant sides under arsene wenger the formation was put to good use and though we have seen much less of this formation used in recent seasons big sides such as juventus and atletico madrid continue to deploy this shape with relative success but of course 442 is not as popular as it once was with many coaches prioritizing an extra man in central midfield instead of two strikers still the formation can be effective when used properly when the strengths of the shape are emphasized and the weaknesses are minimized so how does that work one of 442's biggest strengths is the simplicity in player roles compared to other formations though specific requirements always depend on team principles there tends to be an ease of implementing this formation at various levels of the game though the flip side of this can be a potential lack of dynamism the simple nature of the 442 also leads to a natural equilibrium within the structure the symmetrical shape offers a balance to the side both when defending and attacking allowing for the midfield line of four to offer support in both phases another extremely useful advantage is the solidity of the shape when out of possession a 4-4-2 block can be so difficult to break down that many teams will defend using this tactic regardless of the formation they choose to attack with stylistically speaking when lined up appropriately the 442 covers and protects the most space on the pitch compared to any other formation in football with two banks of four and the two strikers up top any team which uses this shape and focuses on vertical and lateral compactness will be difficult to break down the use of wingers and fullbacks in the same formation also offers natural width to the side when in possession doubling up in the wide areas of the pitch particularly when the fullback overlaps can stretch the opposition laterally which will in turn create spaces centrally to attack this could be a factor which leads to a side attempting more crosses throughout the course of a match especially considering that there are often two strikers positioned within the box during the final attacking phase the 442 can also be a wonderful setup for a team looking to counter-attack with regularity with two strikers at the top of the shape there tends to be more forward options to play and to alleviate the pressure from the defenders and midfielders this also means that in contrast to a team playing with a lone striker the forward tandem can play off each other with less responsibility for holding up the ball and linking play their roles are more attacking more based on creating opportunity for one another however the formation has suffered its decline in popularity for a reason it has weaknesses which can be exploited and one of the main reasons why a manager may shy away from the 442 is the lack of numbers in the central areas of the pitch with many teams operating with three central midfielders whether in a 4-3-3 or a 4-2-3-1 using a 4-4-2 will often see the side outnumbered in the middle making it much more difficult to control the rhythm of a match interestingly enough some of the perceived strengths of the system can also be seen as weaknesses the symmetrical shape and simplicity in roles can lead to a different set of problems the flat nature of the 442 means that in possession there is a lack of natural passing angles and passing options compared to other setups and when out of possession the two banks of four may become too flat making it easier for the opposition to play through the lines as opposed to a shape which is more staggered though perhaps more common at the lower levels of the game a 442 system also runs the risk of becoming stretched and the lines disconnected from each other without the proper discipline from the four midfield players the 4-4-2 can quickly turn into what looks more like a 4-2-4 both in and out of possession leaving two central players even more isolated with the responsibility of covering the entirety of the midfield this classic formation still has its place in modern football and also comes with a few variations with one of the strikers dropping off it can quickly turn into a 4-4-1-1 or the midfield shape can also be shifted into a diamond with one of the central midfielders playing ahead of the other as with any formation player instructions and roles will vary from coach to coach and the players that they have at their disposal with the creation of a good belgium the 343 has become an intriguing option for any side looking for a solid balance between defense and attack whether referred to as a back three or a back five it's widely accepted that systems which employ three centre-backs increased in popularity and usage during the 1980s with most teams utilizing two strikers against the two centre-backs the addition of a third central defender allowed for a spare man in defence for extra cover there are different types of through the back system but the 343 is the most common with its three center backs two modern wing backs a double pivot two free roaming tens and a striker but what are the natural advantages and disadvantages that come with the 343 this is a formation which offers a well-balanced setup with many sides choosing to create a structure in possession which allows for five players to attack and five players to maintain balance the three-two shape at the back which is created by the three central defenders and the double pivot is a great foundation the front five is then created by the two wing backs the two attacking midfielders and the striker with the wing backs maintaining width on each side to stretch the opposition laterally and the striker making runs in behind the back line to stretch them vertically there will then be spaces opened between the lines for the attacking midfielders to operate in depending on their role within the team the wing-backs in a 3-4-3 can be utilized in various ways which is something that can allow the system a degree of tactical flexibility in possession they will often have the freedom to both push forward simultaneously knowing they have defensive coverage behind them in the form of three center backs this allows for the side in possession to hold width on each side and always have a threat on the back post and when the team is out of possession the wing backs can be deployed in varying roles as well a team looking to press the opposition high up the pitch can push the wing backs forward allowing for a more aggressive approach in a high block or in the instances that the team gets pushed back into their low block shape the wing backs can drop back into the back line creating a five man defense the natural width provided by the wing backs in the attack and the addition of the attacking midfielders drifting wide creating overloads in wide areas of the pitch is often a key component of breaking down the opposition creating situations in wide areas of the pitch which can shift the opposition block from one side to another will also allow for quick switches of play to the opposite flank where the other wingback can find themselves in a 1v1 or 2v1 situation this is a concept which is typically known as overload to isolate and is a very viable way of creating chances through this system rotations amongst the front three is also a common approach for teams setting up in a 3-4-3 whether that means two players stretching the back line with one player dropping underneath one player up top with two players finding space between the lines or one of the attacking midfielders dropping even deeper into the midfield to create central overloads there are many positional rotations which can occur within this structure one final key foundation of this formation which is important in bull progression chance creation and counter pressing is the strength of the box shape created by the double pivot and the attacking midfielders cohesion among these four players is a component for success now while the 343 offers an array of strengths it's not to say that the formation is without potential deficiencies any formation in modern football which lines up with just two natural central midfielders will always run the risk of being outnumbered in the center of the pitch which could make it difficult to control the tempo of the match the space being seated on the wings on the outside of the center backs is another potential issue with both wing backs pushing up into the attack these wide areas may become susceptible to opposition counter attacks this will require the wide centre-backs to be mobile and capable of covering larger areas of space and defending one-on-one in wider areas of the pitch when compared to a more traditional centre-back pair the wide center-backs will also have more responsibility to progress the ball into midfield whether that's through carries or line-breaking passes finding defenders who possess the necessary attributes and are capable of this role can also present challenges and great cost positioning for the two players who are deployed in the double pivot may also be an area for concern if they are not disciplined it's often up to them to maintain a sense of balance in the side both in and out of possession and a lapse in judgment by these players could leave the back line exposed while some may choose to call it a 541 or a 3421 the 343 has become a fashionable system for many top sides and coaches a formation which offers balance and can be exciting going forwards while also maintaining strong foundations for defending at the back it may require players who are more title: Why Teams Play With a Back Three
content: you can now get a 30-day trial to experience the athletic for free visit the link in the description below to try it now why do teams play with the back three well of the many reasons the most obvious is that the shape helps create numerical advantages in defensive situations which makes teams more defensively sound it isn't coincidental that some of the supposedly weaker sides in euro 2020 have opted for a three-man defensive system with finland north macedonia and hungary all examples of teams who have utilized a 3-5-2 during the tournament this particular formation allows them to force opposition build-up play wide as two strikers block vertical passes three midfielders congest the center of the pitch behind them and the wing backs then gain a 2v1 advantage against an attacking winger if the opposition is able to get the ball into the box from a cross the advantage of playing three central defenders versus two is obvious there is one more body to contest aerial balls therefore making the defense stronger weaker teams tend to select a 3-5-2 or a 3-4-3 because they expect to have less of the ball than their opponents and need to protect against that disparity additionally the most likely way that they can expect to create chances is on the counter-attack so by sitting back and blocking the space then attacking with wing backs and a couple of forwards they maximize their defensive output and exploit an opponent in a vulnerable attacking shape some managers will fit players into a 3-5-2 or 3-4-3 system because it's how they want to play while others select it because it suits the personnel available scotland are an example of this as it helps them get left-back andy robertson in the same starting eleven as fellow left-back kieran tierney but it's not just lower-ranked teams who utilize a three-man defensive shape belgium have spent a long time as the number one rated team in the world and have some of the best players on the planet to choose from so why does coach roberto martinez prefer a 343 well one reason might be that in order to play the sort of possession-based high-press attacking game he wants to it's essential to ensure that there is defensive balance or at least a safety net to guard against the counter-attack playing a 3-4-3 means that not only do they benefit from the same advantages as weaker sides i.e being far harder to break down and score against when out of possession but because they're so good in attacking situations that they can enjoy the best of both worlds belgium have central defenders comfortable on the ball who can play passes out from the back or carry it into midfield to help create overloads the wing-backs can get further up the pitch from a higher starting position than full-backs requiring less defensive cover from midfielders which helps gain control of opposition territory now one negative is that playing an extra centre-back means losing a more creative player higher up the pitch but in tentative kg international games the more defensively solid teams have something of an advantage look at greece in 2004 or portugal in 2016 for winning examples it only takes one goal to win a game after all and for some teams that's precisely what they're looking for and of course a back three doesn't necessarily mean a team is defensive johan cruyff's incredible netherlands team of 1974 nearly perfected total football using one and pep guardiola's manchester city regularly transitioned from a back four to a three in an increasingly common shape seen used by italy at euro 2020 as one fullback tucks in and another advances some managers are using three five two and three four three formations to help in build up most use them because they help weaker size defending greater numbers to frustrate superior opponents and of course it's far easier to destroy than create so for some teams their best chance of winning is by blocking and stopping the opposition hoping the few title: Atalanta Tactics Explained
content: Atalanta have continued to deliver in this season serie jumpier Gasparini has followed up last season's third-place finish by guiding the Bergamo bass club to fourth place so far with Champions League football yet again on the horizon Atalanta are probably Syria's most tactically complex side for all the consistency of their three four one two or three four to one setups they run myriad variations of plays within them gas Perini's acumen has seen the front players especially excel attacking midfielder pappu Gomes and forwards Luis Muriel Devan Zapata and the athletics area player of the season Yosef illogic have scored 45 legals between them they've combined to make Atalanta the highest scoring team in the league and the third highest overall in Europe's top five leagues at the lander have scored ten goals more than the next most prolific Italian side Lazio and they take a lot of shots per game two more than any other side in the league but they've developed a style that allows them consistently to work the ball into dangerous positions shot volume counts for little if the shots are of poor quality guess farini's team looked to attack the wide areas and half spaces generating overloads through combination play involving defence midfield and attack they play least through the center where Gomes has something of a free roll we'll break down some of the more usual attacking patterns of play but this is a team with a lot of variations and players who can respond to situations creatively this is part of their danger it's possible to understand how Atalanta play but players like Gomes analytic add a degree of spontaneity and improvisation that makes them very hard to stop Atalanta standard 3 4 1 2 naturally lends their approach plate with the wing backs rub in Horsens on the left and hans hatter Bua on the right offer this naturally while both central midfielders drift out to support this and one of the forwards will also pull wide towards the side where the ball is this means Atalanta can have four or five players occupying wide areas but they also maintain their width irrespective of which side of the pitch the ball is on this allows for switches in play through the uncongested center and causes opposition defences problems as they try to adjust while the creative players naturally get the plaudits the system functions well because Atalanta have a number of extremely hard-working tactically intelligent midfielders players like Martin Darren Ramallah and Maria Pechaluk these players glue the elements of Atlanta's transitional play together shifting their position in relation to the movements of the wing backs and forwards to ensure that there are always passing options if the side are looking to retain possession and build from the back the midfielder will drop into space in the channel and add a passing point this allows the wider center back to push forwards to cover the advancing wing back if the wide center back carries the ball forwards the central midfielder may stay in position and allow the side to retain its defensive shape the central midfielders will push up and wider though if the center backs hold their position and if a centre forward drops off to linked play is not uncommon to see the central midfielder push beyond them especially Pechaluk this ensures that Atalanta can have a rough three-to-five shape in possession irrespective of which players are actually the ones who push forwards it demands a lot of the midfield filling in or connecting play or making runs depending on what else is happening on the pitch outside them the wing backs do mostly stay wide but will cut infield and offer an option in the half space especially if the forwards are pulling wide to make space for a run from midfield and even the center backs usually bare at Jim City Jose Luis Palomino and Rafael Tolo are involved in this desire to overload the wide and half spaces they will carry the ball forwards or make runs into attacking possessions covered by the midfield especially if room is created by a forward pulling wide they also space very wide across the backline so that the wing backs and wide center backs may occupy the same horizontal space covered by a midfielder dropping in this means that it's easy to generate overloads and stretch the opposition defense into wide areas leaving gaps elsewhere the position switching movement of the other midfielders in the forwards then pulls the opposition defense in various directions meaning that Atalanta either create space for players in dangerous positions or make room for runs that penetrate the opposition box all these rotations and movements serve to create space for the front two and Gomez who is often the only player genuinely central apart from the central center back and goalkeeper in a fascinating interview with el pase Gomez explains that the referee is often his point of reference who's best placed in the whole field the referee he's always alone Gomez his role is to find this space he stitches play together dropping deep to collect the ball and shift it wide pushing up into the half spaces to act as the free man or create a passing triangle or arriving late to exploit the space created by others to shoot or assist the forwards Zapata analytic do roam to a degree but they will also spend time in the wide channels creating space for runs from deep both forwards and Gomez will also drive forwards play quick one-twos and switch the angle of attack from a half space into the center quickly and at the Lancers retention of width means that if for example the left side is attacked and then the ball is played across the center a player is often able to enter the box unmarked on the right-hand side and score rather llantas quick exchanges in the box are part of the reason that they have almost 100 more touches in the box this season than the next best team napoli the for all Atlanta's undoubted brilliance in attack from open play they also possess good set piece takers especially illa touch and sapota is excellent in the air only Roma have scored as many as Atalanta from set pieces in the league 11 while they're attacking metrics like progressive or key passes are all excellent and they're the fourth best team for possession and passes per minute they are defensively sound - this is partly because they see so much of the ball and partly because their ability to transition makes teams wary of committing too much to attacks although they are certainly more vulnerable to teams who match their three of the back set but no team has conceded viewer shots against than Atalanta while their third four interceptions and for PPD a the measure that shows how much sides press Atalanta are a superb team full of talented players many of whom are performing beyond what might previously have been expected of them tenacious and resilient in defense full of purpose and intelligence in attack Atalanta under gasparini are showing that an innovative tactical approach can deliver if you liked today's video you can read much more coverage of italian football by joining us at the athletic and following the almighty james horn castle subscribing to the athletic is the best way to support TFO and crucially you can try it for free by clicking the link below thank you for your support

title: Tactics Explained: Roma
content: in-depth football coverage from the athletic is now just one pound per week see the link in the description to sign up today under paolo fonseca roma have been playing exciting football this season i'd put them with atalanta and sasuolo as the league's entertainers says the athletics james horncastle and understandably so with a balanced squad of developing talent and hardened experience roma are making strides in both serie and in europe under a highly capable but still unheralded coach fonseca has been the manager of roma since the summer of 2019. he enjoyed a hugely successful stint at shakhtar donetsk where he won the double in each of his three seasons in charge during this period fonsecas shakhtar met napoli and roma in continental competitions giving both a tough time which drew him to the attention of italian football fonseca is a disciple of vitorfrada's tactical periodization also famously espoused by jose mourinho carlos kirosh and other portuguese coaches this method creates training schedules based on the idea that physical and technical work must coincide in each session that working with the ball at all times conditions players to respond to situations as they would in a match context it aims to make players more comfortable on the ball and at greater ease using it in situations of high physical stress fonseca is also an intense presence on the training pitch and his methods are clearly paying off as roma's defenders especially have become more comfortable on the ball and the team is becoming increasingly adept at playing his style of football fonseca started off at roma with a 4-2-3-1 or a 4-3-3 his favored system at shakhtar the two nil copper italia win in january last year saw the debut of a three at the back but it wasn't until july that fonseca committed to a tactical shift that saw one loss to napoli but then an unbeaten serie a run of eight games including a 3-1 away win at juventus this season fonseca has almost exclusively stayed with the 3-4-3 this system sees the back three split wide in build up assisted by the goalkeeper paul lopez so that the shape can look like a flatish back four one midfielder usually drops off two creating a forward passing option in front of the back three or they will drop into the position of one of the centre-backs usually on the left side while that centre-back holds an even wider position and one of the most interesting developments has actually been fonseca's use of brian cristante as a centre-back cristante came from atalanta as a midfielder albeit a creative deep lying one but fonseca has refashioned him into a ball playing center half who sits in the middle of the back three it's a change that has provided the team with enhanced passing options from deep and a central centre-back who can push up into the midfield line to give them greater control over weaker teams fonseca has also worked hard to improve the confidence on the ball of roma's other centre-backs and now in ibanez marash kamboula and the more aggressive gianluca mancini roma have a fleet of intelligent young defenders comfortable in possession and this is important because fonseca favors a buildup of short passes out from the back with players finding space behind the opponent's defensive lines roma don't usually pass long tending only to favour this approach against very good sides who press high it's a style of build-up that favors roma's technical attacking players who are adept at finding space especially the wide attackers the wide players cut in field and leave space for the wing backs to overlap meaning that the attacking front unit of the 343 is often quite narrow eden jeko is moving towards the end of his career but remains a useful focal point he uses his strength and understated passing ability to hold up the ball and then lay off or play through for runners from deep this has benefited the dynamic box-to-box midfielder jourdatu whose late runs have already seen him achieve the best scoring season of his career so far and reached double figures for the first time behind gekko the experienced and creative pedro and henrikh mkhitaryan buzz around looking to carve out passing chances carry the ball or shoot themselves mkhitaryan will generally drift into a more central position and act as a playmaker between the lines while pedro looks to run in behind but the attacking unit is fluid roma have tended to focus their attacking effort centrally looking to overload in that area the wide attackers like to drift in field into the half spaces and width is maintained by using those overlapping wing backs usually the dynamic leonardo spinazzola and rick kashtop they are covered by the wide split of the centre-backs who also offer a useful rotation option should the wing back run into trouble and if they do so roma are unafraid to pass all the way back and restart their patient possession focus build up but the key to their attack is the fluidity and movement of the wide attackers supported by those deep runs from vera to gonzalo via or lorenzo pellegrini pellegrini is an all-around attacking threat recast from playing as a 10 to a deeper role but still with the ability to create chances from very little and the energy to get onto opportunities provided by others roma's ability to generate these central overloads and put runners in behind defenses or quickly move the play to a wing back who crosses back in is what makes them so exciting to watch they have players who can carry the ball effectively through the middle but who also possess the technical ability to create through quick passes which profit from their dynamic runners this should be enhanced further with the return from injury at some point of nicola zagnola another extremely technical midfielder who scored six league goals last season and was linked with a number of top european clubs prior to suffering the second cruciate ligament injury of his career back in september defensively roma press in a situational way the triggers include passes backwards the opponent carrying a ball to a certain height on the pitch and passes from the center backs to the full backs in slightly higher positions the press is generally man orientated and aimed at smothering the opposition and preventing them from breaking forwards roma generally don't counterpress that much preferring to hold their position and use triggers to pressure the ball rather than losing their shape otherwise they seek to block up the center of the pitch often retaining the 343 shape sometimes with one wide attacker coming centrally to mark the opposition's defensive midfielder within serie a roma have also achieved the second most shot and goal creations from defensive actions showing that their intelligent pressing and ability to turn blocks tackles and interceptions directly into attacks is a potent weapon for the side despite not utilizing a frenzied counter press nasseria is likely out of reach for them this season but under fonseca and with a squad that is sharing real signs of improvement under his coaching methods roma are growing towards something key attacking players will admittedly have to be replaced at some point but the foundations of this side are promising and the future does look bright for a club who are now without a title: Tactics Explained: Sassuolo
content: in-depth football coverage from the athletic is now just one pound per week see the link in the description to sign up today roberto de serbi is currently one of the most interesting and innovative coaches in world football despite a relatively unremarkable cv his sasuolo team have grown increasingly impressive during his tenure and sat second in serie after seven games played and while his critics suggest his teams can't defend and that his attacking play is too intricate and showy sasuolo have nonetheless been very effective as the athletic serie correspondent james horncastle explains it's a nonsense there is always a name behind the aesthetic at zazuola de zerby's strategy is holistic intricate build up play under pressure and in tight spaces should improve a player's technique it encourages them to take responsibility and when a move like this comes off it boosts self-esteem that's the multiplier effect at the core of desebby's philosophy what is especially interesting is what deserve does differently to what we might expect from teams playing his favored system the 4231 and the structure he was forced to employ against napoli the 3-4-3 sasuolo are a side who tried to retain possession and make a lot of passes according to statsbomb they've made the most short passes in seria so far this season and the second most between 15 and 30 yards and only six teams have tried fewer long passes or passes over 30 yards this style of football requires a lot of movement and ball rotation and this starts at the back now in a normal 4-2-3-1 one of the midfield pair generally drops in to offer a passing option to the centre-backs or keeper while the full-backs push high and offer width and the wide forwards tuck in this creates a sort of staggered 3-4-3 zazuolo's full-backs do not while they do play wide they don't advance high as part of the build up in their half remaining closer to the center halves instead with the more advanced wide players providing width from the touchline crucially the midfield usually stay behind the opposition first line of defense sasuelo actively invite the press in order to play through it rotating the ball through the defenders and using the goalkeeper andrea concilli as an additional passing option especially very deep this allows sasuolo to progress the ball vertically to the midfield once the opportunity arises finding either manuel ocatelli the team's hub or pedro ubayang in the space between the lines these two play unusually close together maximizing the opportunity to find each other with safe passes should they receive the ball and this was also the case when sasuela used the 343 with the back five creating a kind of empty box shape in possession to allow the midfield to stay up although on occasion lucatelli would drop in if the side were struggling to progress the ball sasuelo's passing especially the wall passes affected when the centre-back passes to a midfielder who then passes to the other centre-back is able to shift the opposition and open spaces once the midfield are in space they can then spread the ball wide and bring the wingers into play sasuolo are a wide attacking team with the attacking midfielder usually philip burech and the prolific center forward francesco caputo looking to hit the box from deep as much as possible rather than holding the ball up and playing others in however they are not a crossing side despite developing their attacks from white in the final third they are most proficient when working the ball into the area through a series of quick passes and runs in behind defenders again according to statsbomb only four sides have made fewer completed crosses into the penalty area than sasuolo and all four make considerably fewer passes anyway so while the wingers stay wide this is to stretch the opposition and allow them to receive the ball in space or create space centrally if a defender is dragged over either way the wingers will then look to play it back into the midfielders who advance or to durachich or caputo once asuelo have established themselves in the opposition half in this way they try to play quickly through and across using the passing options afforded by a kind of staggered 235 shape to get in behind the opposition the skill and dynamism of the wide players jeremy bogar and dominica bharati is crucial here as are the runs of yurochic and caputo and this is the technical intricacy and build up in tight spaces referred to by james horncastle sasuelo are probably the most tactically and technically exciting side in italy after atalanta there are vulnerabilities of course as this commitment to attacking football can allow them to be countered but for a side without many star names lok italian bharatiya's side even caputo is still under appreciated despite his 21 goals last season sasuelo and de zebi are innovative exciting and crucially successful tifo is delighted to be able to title: Diego Simeone's Atletico Madrid Explained
content: diego simeone took over atlético madrid in December 2011 winning the Europa League at the end of that season he offense guided the club to a La Liga title in 2013-14 as well as winning the Copa del Rey the Supercopa de españa the UEFA Super Cup and twice finishing as runners-up of the Champions League Simeone Atletico the most revered as a defensive sign incredibly well organized and hard-working Simeone prefers a 4-4-2 although this season in La Liga he has used a four-for-one one and even a 4-2-3-1 Varian two banks of four is however the template for his system in a league that otherwise tends to prefer 4-2-3-1 or variants of a 5 3 to firstly and with echoes of Arrigo sakis AC Milan side Simeone YZ 442 is both vertically compact and narrow this creates two elements that are key to the team's defensive methodology a congested midfield and overloads outline the central midfielders usually Gabby and the superb coach a drop slightly as do strikers and two in Griezmann and Kevin Camaro who allow the opposition centre backs or center half some space the wide players push up slightly creating something akin to a 4-2 - to this compacts the central area and even though it allows the opposition space to pass the ball they are doing so in areas that cannot hurt Atletico as the opposition moves forward into their defensive third they drop deeper and the wide men stand out slightly the aim is to ensure that when the opposition get to within about 10 yards of the penalty box Madrid have a compact narrow two lines of thought with one striker assisting the midfield and one lurking for the long counter attacking ball Simeone team are all about minimizing risk even if that means ceding possession and it only when the ball moves into dangerous areas that they swarm the opposition and attempt to win possession as Africa Madrid did not press with the same regularity and other sides known for the tactic but when they do its aggressive and successful with the shape sacred above all else the club tend to press only when an opposition player takes a poor touch or when the compact narrow defensive shape has pushed them wider in this instance a winger and a fullback assisted by a forward dropping beep or occasionally a central midfielder shifting across will form the triangle press around the opposition player in possession the whole team will shift across in his instance keeping the overall shape and conscious that the likelihood of the pressed player being able to switch the ball to the more open opposite frame is now limited Atletico Madrid are ruthless on the counter and in m2n Greeson they have a lethally clinical striker Madrid focus the bulk of their attacks from out wide with only around 25% of their attacks starting centrally winning possession from the press the full-backs and winners will drive forwards before looking to release the strikers unless he has been caught offside 3.8 times a match in league of this season more than any other side indicative of their fast breaking approach with this style the team relied much more on individual attacking Flair to create chances as opposed to complex passing moves Diego Simeone has fashioned a side that like sakis or those of josie marino is defensively predicated on rigid organisation intelligent passing and tactical disciplines that maximize attacking chances while minimizing risk Tulisa MO as some call Simeone his approach balances individual skill with team instructions and with this he has created a fearsome team if you'd like to read more of Alex Stewart's writing title: Maurizio Sarri's Napoli Tactics Explained
content: last season Napoli finished second in Syria under their then new manager maritzio sari since sari's appointment Napoli have scored over two goals per game in the league and are generally considered to be playing the most attractive football in Syria sari has also overcome the loss of leading scorer Gonzalo higu to Rivals Juventus and his ability to get the most out of an attacking Trident of Lorenzo inia Ras merens and Jose Callahan has been a significant feature of Napoli's incisive attacking play Napoli line up in a fairly Orthodox 433 which becomes a 451 in defensive posture they press aggressively in the opponent's half following the ball and aiming to cut off the opposition's passing angles when in possession Napoli play a high defensive line which assists this High Press Pepe Raina sweeps competently behind although they occasionally get into trouble against quicker forwards The High Line allows for compactness in the opposition half as the Press is engaged Napoli can avoid too much space appearing because the defense are so far up that the opposition is forced to pass backwards or sideways Napoli aim to win possession back quickly or at the very least force their opposition back or into an error for sari two principles are key Above All Else verticality and possession Napoli are geared up to keep the ball and move it forwards with intensity if the option is not there they'll recycle the ball until it is Napoli build patiently from the back Raina plays short from goal kicks or when he has possession from open play with koui Bal and R albiol giving short options and youro or defensive Midfield Prospect amadu diara a deep Ling playmaker dropping in as well this movement forms at least a triangle if not several and all four players are comfortable taking the ball and playing it round this serves two purposes firstly it lurs the opposition Striker or Strikers into the Press which ties them out and disrupts their own first defensive line secondly it can pull the opposition midfielders forwards as well which then leaves Mar hamik or Alan with Space Between the Lines if the short ball option is uded by an opposition player gulam and husai or the other fullbacks can push or drop to give Raina or the center backs a wider option as Napoli progressed the ball vertically these players also provide width as the team morphs into something of a 2143 in attack often focusing on the left side verticality is key for sari and Napoli's attacking system is predicated on players finding the space to offer vertical passing Lanes inia is a gifted inside forward given license to drift into the half spaces and without the requirement to stay wide width instead comes from the fullbacks especially the dynamic gulam on the left and Jose Callahan who is a more traditional Winger on the right Napoli attack preferentially through the half spaces and focus mostly on the left hand side where their most technically Adept players line up they focus on retaining possession with quick incisive passes and movement to open up triangular passing Lanes this creates angled vertical passing options relying on the technical abilities of players to retain possession Under Pressure while working the ball around to create overloads between the lines incor hamik and merens are the main beneficiaries of this approach and have scored 34
